newsitem.title: USA: Hard rain hits U.S. Northwest hydroelectric system.
newsitem.headline: Hard rain hits U.S. Northwest hydroelectric system.

text.p: Heavy rain and wet snow overnight in the Pacific Northwest has begun to taper off and is not expected to have a big impact on hydroelectric operations, regional industry sources said Tuesday.
But space was cleared in some reservoirs in preparation for possible flooding.

A source at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in Portland, Ore., said most precipitation will drain into the Willamette River rather than the Columbia, which has the region's biggest concentration of large hydroelectric projects.
Extra water from reservoirs at Grand Coulee and John Day, on the Columbia, was discharged overnight in order to make room for possible inflows, a spokeswoman for the Corps said.
The storm has caused power outages in the Portland area, although local utilities could not be immediately reached for details.
Flows through the Willamette's smaller dam projects, such as Hills Creek, Cottage Grove and Fall Creek, have been reduced or shut off for flood control, the Corps said.
A spokeswoman for the Bonneville Power Administration said flooding was widespread along the Willamette, but no details were available about power generation.
